sources.citation: Adamou, Evangelia. 2025. The Popolocan languages. (halshs-03153566), sec. 2.5 Stress.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Surveys stress in Metzontla (penultimate), Atzingo and Tlacoyalco Popoloca (lengthening), Mazatec (final), Ixcatec; says nothing about Western/Ahuatempan Popoloca.

sources.citation: DiCanio, Christian & Ryan Bennett. 2018 preprint (2020). Prosody in Mesoamerican languages (Oxford Handbook of Language Prosody).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Popolocan stress table cites Metzontla (stem-penultimate), Atzingo and Tlacoyalco (variable); Western Popoloca / Ahuatempan not covered.

sources.citation: van der Hulst, Harry, Keren Rice & Leo Wetzels. 2010. The languages of Middle America. In H. van der Hulst, R. Goedemans & E. van Zanten (eds.), A survey of word accentual patterns in the languages of the world, 249-312. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. p. 267 (sec. 5.1.5.1 Chocho-Popolocan).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Second-hand, and about the sister variety: "In Western Popoloca (Williams and E. Pike 1968: 379), the stressed syllable usually, but not always, coincides with the end of the grammatical stem." Williams & Pike's data are from San Felipe Otlaltepec (sanf1264), not Ahuatempan; nothing on Ahuatempan itself.

sources.citation: [Instituto Lingüístico de Verano]. 1994. Alfabeto: popoloca de Ahuatempan. México, D.F.: ILV. 4 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 56498; downloaded via Internet Archive copy of sil.org reapdata PDF)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Four-page alphabet chart (letters a.. y, chr, xr, saltillo) with two example words each and Spanish glosses; macron/acute/tilde diacritics appear on the Popoloca words but are nowhere explained; no text on accent, stress or tone.

sources.note: Only substantial ILV publication on the Ahuatempan variety itself; a 55-page primer by the SIL team (Kalstrom, Austin) may carry notes explaining the acute/macron diacritics (tone vs. accent) seen in the 1994 Alfabeto.

sources.citation: Kalstrom (Dolson), Marjorie R. & Jeanne Austin (Krumholz). ca. 1985-1995. Unpublished field materials on Ahuatempan Popoloca (phonology statement / orthography proposal), SIL Mexico branch archive.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Kalstrom (author of the 1968 Eastern Popoloca stress paper) and Austin ran the ILV Ahuatempan literacy programme 1986-1995; an internal phonology/orthography statement is the most likely place an Ahuatempan stress rule was ever written down. Existence unverified.

sources.citation: Williams, Ann F. & Eunice V. Pike. 1968. The phonology of Western Popoloca. Lingua 20: 368-380 (stress on p. 379).

sources.note: Only published phonology of Western Popoloca (the two-member subgroup Otlaltepec + Ahuatempan); need p. 379 verbatim and to check whether any Ahuatempan data are included or whether it is Otlaltepec-only (SIL record says Otlaltepec).
